description: Design a curriculum from needs assessment through alignment matrix to final document.

steps.description: Conduct a needs assessment covering learner profiles, prerequisite skills, and industry requirements.

inputs.name: program-scope
inputs.desc: Subject area and target learner population

outputs.name: needs-assessment-report
outputs.desc: Summary of learner needs and skill gaps

outputs.name: learner-profile
outputs.desc: Composite profile of the target learner

process: Survey the target learner population for existing skills and goals
Analyze industry and professional standards for required competencies
Identify the gap between current skills and required outcomes
Produce the needs assessment report with prioritized gaps

steps.description: Define measurable learning outcomes aligned to standards and needs assessment findings.

inputs.name: needs-assessment-report
inputs.desc: Summary of learner needs and skill gaps

outputs.name: learning-outcomes-list
outputs.desc: List of measurable learning outcomes

outputs.name: outcome-standard-map
outputs.desc: Mapping of outcomes to standards

process: Draft learning outcomes using action verbs (Bloom's taxonomy)
Align each outcome to one or more industry standards
Verify outcomes are measurable and assessable
Produce the outcomes list and alignment map

steps.description: Sequence courses and modules into a logical progression from foundational to advanced.

inputs.name: learner-profile
inputs.desc: Composite profile of the target learner

outputs.name: course-sequence
outputs.desc: Ordered list of courses and modules with prerequisites

outputs.name: prerequisite-map
outputs.desc: Dependency graph of course prerequisites

process: Group outcomes by topic and complexity level
Order modules from foundational to advanced
Define prerequisite relationships between courses
Produce the course sequence and prerequisite map

steps.description: Select instructional strategies and materials for each module based on learning outcomes and learner profile.

inputs.name: course-sequence
inputs.desc: Ordered list of courses and modules

outputs.name: strategy-plan
outputs.desc: Instructional strategies mapped to each module

outputs.name: materials-list
outputs.desc: Required materials, textbooks, and resources per module

process: Match each outcome to an instructional method (lecture, lab, project, discussion)
Select primary and supplementary materials for each module
Identify technology and facility requirements
Produce the strategy plan and materials list

steps.description: Design the assessment plan with formative and summative assessments for each outcome.

inputs.name: course-sequence
inputs.desc: Ordered list of courses and modules

outputs.name: assessment-plan
outputs.desc: Formative and summative assessments per module

outputs.name: assessment-calendar
outputs.desc: Timeline of all assessments

process: Design formative assessments (quizzes, reflections, peer review) for each module
Design summative assessments (exams, projects, portfolios) for each course
Schedule assessments across the program timeline
Produce the assessment plan and calendar

steps.description: Build the curriculum alignment matrix mapping outcomes to courses, strategies, and assessments.

inputs.name: assessment-plan
inputs.desc: Formative and summative assessments per module

inputs.name: strategy-plan
inputs.desc: Instructional strategies mapped to each module

outputs.name: alignment-matrix
outputs.desc: Matrix showing outcome-course-assessment-strategy alignment

outputs.name: curriculum-document
outputs.desc: Final curriculum document ready for review

process: Cross-reference each outcome against courses, strategies, and assessments
Identify any outcomes without adequate assessment coverage
Fill gaps and finalize the alignment matrix
Compile the full curriculum document

description: Develop a single lesson plan from objectives through activities to formative assessment.

steps.description: Identify and write the learning objectives for one lesson session.

inputs.name: topic
inputs.desc: The subject and topic for this lesson

inputs.name: prior-knowledge
inputs.desc: What learners already know coming into this lesson

outputs.name: lesson-objectives
outputs.desc: Specific, measurable objectives for this lesson

outputs.name: success-criteria
outputs.desc: Observable criteria indicating the objectives are met

process: Identify 2-4 learning objectives for the session
Write each objective with an action verb and measurable criterion
Define observable success criteria for each objective

steps.description: Design the opening activity to activate prior knowledge and engage learners.

inputs.name: lesson-objectives
inputs.desc: Specific, measurable objectives for this lesson

inputs.name: prior-knowledge
inputs.desc: What learners already know coming into this lesson

outputs.name: opening-activity
outputs.desc: Description of the hook and prior knowledge activation

outputs.name: opening-materials
outputs.desc: Materials needed for the opening activity

process: Design a hook to capture attention (question, scenario, demonstration)
Plan an activity to activate relevant prior knowledge
Estimate timing (5-10 minutes)
List required materials

steps.description: Plan the core instructional activities: direct instruction, guided practice, and independent work.

inputs.name: lesson-objectives
inputs.desc: Specific, measurable objectives for this lesson

inputs.name: opening-activity
inputs.desc: Description of the hook and prior knowledge activation

outputs.name: activity-sequence
outputs.desc: Ordered list of instructional activities with timing

outputs.name: activity-materials
outputs.desc: Materials and resources for each activity

process: Plan the direct instruction segment (explanation, modeling)
Design guided practice with scaffolding
Design independent practice or application activity
Assign time estimates to each segment

steps.description: Prepare all materials, handouts, slides, and technology resources for the lesson.

inputs.name: activity-sequence
inputs.desc: Ordered list of instructional activities with timing

inputs.name: activity-materials
inputs.desc: Materials and resources for each activity

outputs.name: resource-package
outputs.desc: All prepared materials ready for the lesson

outputs.name: technology-checklist
outputs.desc: Technology setup checklist

process: Prepare handouts, worksheets, and reference materials
Create or select presentation slides
Verify technology requirements (projector, software, internet)
Produce the resource package and tech checklist

steps.description: Design the formative assessment to check understanding during or at the end of the lesson.

inputs.name: lesson-objectives
inputs.desc: Specific, measurable objectives for this lesson

inputs.name: success-criteria
inputs.desc: Observable criteria indicating the objectives are met

outputs.name: formative-assessment
outputs.desc: Assessment task (exit ticket, quiz, demonstration)

outputs.name: assessment-key
outputs.desc: Answer key or scoring guide

process: Select an assessment format aligned to the objectives (exit ticket, quick quiz, think-pair-share)
Write the assessment items or prompts
Create the answer key or scoring guide
Plan how to use results for next-lesson adjustments

steps.description: Compile all components into the final lesson plan document with timing and transitions.

inputs.name: opening-activity
inputs.desc: Description of the hook and prior knowledge activation

inputs.name: activity-sequence
inputs.desc: Ordered list of instructional activities with timing

outputs.name: lesson-plan
outputs.desc: Complete lesson plan document

outputs.name: lesson-timeline
outputs.desc: Minute-by-minute timeline of the lesson

process: Assemble all sections into the lesson plan template
Add transitions between activities
Finalize the minute-by-minute timeline
Review for alignment between objectives, activities, and assessment

description: Create and validate an assessment rubric with defined criteria, quality levels, and inter-rater calibration.

steps.description: Identify the learning outcomes and performance dimensions the rubric will assess.

inputs.name: assignment-description
inputs.desc: Description of the assignment or task being assessed

inputs.name: learning-outcomes
inputs.desc: The outcomes this assignment is designed to measure

outputs.name: performance-dimensions
outputs.desc: List of dimensions to evaluate

outputs.name: dimension-definitions
outputs.desc: Clear definition of each dimension

process: Analyze the assignment for distinct performance aspects
Map each aspect to one or more learning outcomes
Define each dimension clearly and without overlap

steps.description: Write quality level descriptors for each performance dimension.

outputs.name: rubric-draft
outputs.desc: Draft rubric with all levels described

outputs.name: level-scale
outputs.desc: The scale used (e.g., exemplary, proficient, developing, beginning)

process: Define the scale levels (typically 3-5 levels)
Write descriptors for the highest level first
Write descriptors for the lowest level
Fill in intermediate levels with clear distinctions between adjacent levels

steps.description: Assign weights to each dimension based on its importance to the learning outcomes.

inputs.name: rubric-draft
inputs.desc: Draft rubric with all levels described

inputs.name: learning-outcomes
inputs.desc: The outcomes this assignment is designed to measure

outputs.name: weighted-rubric
outputs.desc: Rubric with dimension weights assigned

outputs.name: weight-rationale
outputs.desc: Justification for the weight distribution

process: Rank dimensions by importance to the learning outcomes
Assign percentage or point weights
Verify weights sum to 100% and reflect priorities
Document the rationale for weight choices

steps.description: Pilot the rubric on sample student work to identify ambiguities and scoring issues.

inputs.name: assignment-description
inputs.desc: Description of the assignment or task being assessed

outputs.name: pilot-results
outputs.desc: Scores and notes from pilot testing

outputs.name: ambiguity-log
outputs.desc: List of unclear or problematic descriptors

process: Select 5-10 sample student submissions spanning quality levels
Score each sample using the rubric
Note any descriptors that are ambiguous or hard to apply
Record the scoring results and issues found

steps.description: Calibrate the rubric across multiple raters to establish inter-rater reliability.

inputs.name: pilot-results
inputs.desc: Scores and notes from pilot testing

outputs.name: calibrated-rubric
outputs.desc: Revised rubric after calibration

outputs.name: reliability-score
outputs.desc: Inter-rater reliability metric (e.g., Cohen's kappa)

process: Have 2-3 raters independently score the same samples
Compute inter-rater agreement (Cohen's kappa or percentage agreement)
Discuss and resolve disagreements
Revise descriptors that caused inconsistent scoring

steps.description: Finalize the rubric document with instructions for use and scoring procedures.

outputs.name: final-rubric
outputs.desc: Validated rubric document ready for use

outputs.name: rubric-guide
outputs.desc: Instructions for raters on applying the rubric

process: Incorporate all revisions from calibration
Write clear instructions for raters
Format the rubric for distribution
Document the validation process and reliability results

description: Prepare for an institutional or program accreditation review from self-study through site visit readiness.

steps.description: Map the accreditation standards to institutional programs and identify responsible parties.

inputs.name: accrediting-body
inputs.desc: Name and standards of the accrediting organization

inputs.name: institution-profile
inputs.desc: Overview of the institution and its programs

outputs.name: standard-map
outputs.desc: Each standard mapped to responsible departments and evidence sources

outputs.name: evidence-checklist
outputs.desc: Checklist of evidence needed per standard

process: List all accreditation standards and sub-standards
Map each standard to the institutional unit responsible
Identify the evidence types required for each standard
Produce the standard map and evidence checklist

steps.description: Conduct the self-study by evaluating institutional compliance against each standard.

inputs.name: standard-map
inputs.desc: Each standard mapped to responsible departments

inputs.name: evidence-checklist
inputs.desc: Checklist of evidence needed per standard

outputs.name: self-study-findings
outputs.desc: Compliance status and evidence for each standard

outputs.name: gap-list
outputs.desc: Standards where evidence is missing or compliance is partial

process: Collect evidence from each responsible unit
Evaluate compliance for each standard (met, partially met, not met)
Document findings with supporting evidence
Identify gaps requiring remediation

steps.description: Remediate identified gaps by developing action plans and collecting missing evidence.

inputs.name: gap-list
inputs.desc: Standards where evidence is missing or compliance is partial

inputs.name: standard-map
inputs.desc: Each standard mapped to responsible departments

outputs.name: remediation-plan
outputs.desc: Action plans for each gap with owners and deadlines

outputs.name: new-evidence
outputs.desc: Newly collected or created evidence for gap standards

process: Prioritize gaps by severity and deadline
Assign remediation owners and set deadlines
Develop or collect the missing evidence
Verify remediation closes each gap

steps.description: Write the self-study report compiling findings, evidence, and remediation for submission.

inputs.name: self-study-findings
inputs.desc: Compliance status and evidence for each standard

inputs.name: new-evidence
inputs.desc: Newly collected evidence for gap standards

outputs.name: self-study-report
outputs.desc: Complete self-study report document

outputs.name: evidence-appendix
outputs.desc: Organized evidence appendix referenced by the report

process: Organize findings by standard in the required format
Integrate evidence references throughout the narrative
Compile the evidence appendix
Review for completeness and accuracy

steps.description: Prepare the institution for the accreditation site visit.

outputs.name: site-visit-plan
outputs.desc: Schedule, logistics, and interview assignments for the visit

outputs.name: accreditation-package
outputs.desc: Final accreditation submission package

process: Organize the evidence room (physical or virtual)
Prepare staff for interviews by standard area
Create the site visit schedule and logistics plan
Compile and submit the final accreditation package

description: Create an online course from objectives and storyboarding through LMS deployment and pilot testing.

steps.description: Define the learning objectives and target audience for the online course.

inputs.name: course-topic
inputs.desc: Subject and scope of the course

outputs.name: course-objectives
outputs.desc: List of learning objectives for the course

outputs.name: audience-analysis
outputs.desc: Analysis of learner characteristics and prerequisites

process: Analyze the target audience (background, motivation, technical access)
Define 5-10 learning objectives for the course
Determine prerequisite knowledge and skills
Set the course scope and estimated duration

steps.description: Storyboard the course modules, sequencing content and activities for each lesson.

outputs.name: course-storyboard
outputs.desc: Module-by-module outline with content types and activities

outputs.name: media-plan
outputs.desc: List of media assets needed (videos, graphics, interactives)

process: Divide objectives into modules of manageable length
Outline each module with content segments and activities
Identify media types for each segment (video, reading, interactive, discussion)
Produce the storyboard and media production plan

steps.description: Produce the course content: video lectures, readings, and interactive elements.

outputs.name: content-assets
outputs.desc: All produced content files (videos, documents, interactives)

outputs.name: content-inventory
outputs.desc: Inventory of all assets with metadata

process: Script and record video lectures
Write or curate reading materials
Build interactive activities and simulations
Catalog all assets in the content inventory

steps.description: Build the course in the learning management system, uploading content and configuring navigation.

outputs.name: lms-course
outputs.desc: Course configured in the LMS and ready for testing

outputs.name: navigation-map
outputs.desc: Map of course structure and navigation paths

process: Create the course shell in the LMS
Upload and organize content by module
Configure navigation, prerequisites, and completion tracking
Set up the discussion forums and communication tools

steps.description: Set up assessments and grading in the LMS for the online course.

outputs.name: assessment-setup
outputs.desc: All assessments configured in the LMS with rubrics

outputs.name: gradebook-config
outputs.desc: Gradebook configuration with weights and policies

process: Create quizzes, assignments, and discussion prompts in the LMS
Upload rubrics and scoring criteria
Configure the gradebook with weights and late policies
Set up automated feedback where possible

steps.description: Pilot the course with a test group and evaluate for usability and learning effectiveness.

outputs.name: pilot-feedback
outputs.desc: Feedback from pilot participants on usability and content

outputs.name: course-package
outputs.desc: Final course package with revisions from pilot

process: Recruit a small pilot group (5-15 learners)
Run the pilot over a compressed timeline
Collect feedback on usability, clarity, engagement, and technical issues
Revise the course based on pilot results and finalize

description: Set up a learning management system from requirements through configuration, migration, and training.

steps.description: Define the LMS requirements covering user roles, content types, integrations, and reporting.

inputs.name: organization-profile
inputs.desc: Size, structure, and learning needs of the organization

inputs.name: existing-systems
inputs.desc: Current systems the LMS must integrate with

outputs.name: lms-requirements
outputs.desc: Prioritized list of functional and technical requirements

outputs.name: integration-needs
outputs.desc: Required integrations (SIS, HR, SSO, content libraries)

process: Interview stakeholders (instructors, admins, learners, IT)
Document functional requirements (enrollment, grading, reporting, content types)
Document technical requirements (SSO, API, mobile, accessibility)
Prioritize requirements as must-have, should-have, nice-to-have

steps.description: Evaluate and select the LMS platform that best fits the requirements.

outputs.name: platform-selection
outputs.desc: Selected LMS platform with justification

outputs.name: comparison-matrix
outputs.desc: Feature comparison across evaluated platforms

process: Identify 3-5 candidate platforms
Score each against the requirements matrix
Evaluate cost (license, hosting, support)
Select the best fit and document the rationale

steps.description: Configure the selected LMS: branding, categories, roles, enrollment rules, and integrations.

outputs.name: configured-lms
outputs.desc: LMS configured and ready for content

outputs.name: configuration-log
outputs.desc: Record of all configuration settings

process: Apply branding (logo, colors, terminology)
Set up user roles and permissions
Configure enrollment rules and course categories
Connect integrations (SSO, SIS, content libraries)

steps.description: Migrate existing course content from legacy systems into the new LMS.

inputs.name: configured-lms
inputs.desc: LMS configured and ready for content

outputs.name: migrated-content
outputs.desc: All content migrated and verified in the new LMS

outputs.name: migration-report
outputs.desc: Report of items migrated, skipped, or requiring manual work

process: Export content from legacy systems (SCORM, files, assessments)
Import into the new LMS using bulk tools or APIs
Verify content renders and functions correctly
Document any items requiring manual recreation

steps.description: Train administrators and instructors on using the new LMS.

outputs.name: training-materials
outputs.desc: User guides and training resources

outputs.name: lms-documentation
outputs.desc: Complete LMS setup and operations documentation

process: Create user guides for each role (admin, instructor, learner)
Conduct training sessions for administrators and instructors
Set up a sandbox environment for practice
Produce the final LMS documentation package

description: Identify at-risk students, assess root causes, intervene, and track outcomes.

steps.description: Identify at-risk students using early warning indicators from institutional data.

inputs.name: student-data
inputs.desc: Enrollment, attendance, grade, and engagement data

inputs.name: risk-thresholds
inputs.desc: Thresholds for flagging students (e.g., below 70%, two missed classes)

outputs.name: at-risk-list
outputs.desc: List of students flagged with their risk indicators

outputs.name: risk-summary
outputs.desc: Summary statistics of at-risk population

process: Pull current data on attendance, grades, and engagement
Apply the risk thresholds to flag students
Categorize by risk level (high, medium, low)
Produce the at-risk list and summary

steps.description: Assess the root causes of academic risk for each flagged student.

inputs.name: at-risk-list
inputs.desc: List of students flagged with their risk indicators

inputs.name: student-data
inputs.desc: Enrollment, attendance, grade, and engagement data

outputs.name: cause-analysis
outputs.desc: Root cause assessment per student (academic, financial, personal, health)

outputs.name: support-needs
outputs.desc: Matched support services needed per student

process: Review each student's academic history and current performance
Identify patterns (specific courses, attendance drops, engagement changes)
Categorize causes: academic skill gaps, financial stress, personal issues, health
Match each student to relevant support services

steps.description: Implement the matched interventions: tutoring, advising, financial aid referrals, or counseling.

inputs.name: support-needs
inputs.desc: Matched support services needed per student

outputs.name: intervention-log
outputs.desc: Record of interventions deployed per student

outputs.name: referral-confirmations
outputs.desc: Confirmations that referrals were received

process: Contact each student and explain available support
Make referrals to tutoring, advising, financial aid, or counseling
Confirm referrals are received and appointments scheduled
Log all interventions in the tracking system

steps.description: Track student progress after intervention to measure improvement.

inputs.name: student-data
inputs.desc: Enrollment, attendance, grade, and engagement data

outputs.name: progress-report
outputs.desc: Progress metrics per student post-intervention

outputs.name: escalation-list
outputs.desc: Students not improving who need additional support

process: Monitor grades, attendance, and engagement at 2-week and 4-week marks
Compare post-intervention metrics to pre-intervention baseline
Flag students showing no improvement for escalation
Produce the progress report

steps.description: Evaluate the overall effectiveness of the intervention program.

outputs.name: effectiveness-report
outputs.desc: Analysis of which interventions produced the best outcomes

outputs.name: program-recommendations
outputs.desc: Recommendations for improving the intervention program

process: Calculate retention and grade improvement rates by intervention type
Compare outcomes for intervened vs. non-intervened students
Identify the most and least effective interventions
Produce recommendations for program improvement

description: Design a faculty development program from needs assessment through evaluation of teaching impact.

steps.description: Assess faculty development needs across teaching, technology, and research.

inputs.name: faculty-roster
inputs.desc: List of faculty with roles, disciplines, and experience levels

inputs.name: institutional-priorities
inputs.desc: Teaching and research priorities of the institution

outputs.name: needs-survey-results
outputs.desc: Aggregated faculty development needs by category

outputs.name: priority-topics
outputs.desc: Ranked list of development topics

process: Survey faculty on self-assessed development needs
Analyze student evaluation data for common areas of concern
Cross-reference with institutional priorities
Rank topics by frequency and institutional alignment

steps.description: Design the workshop and seminar series based on identified faculty needs.

inputs.name: faculty-roster
inputs.desc: List of faculty with roles and disciplines

outputs.name: workshop-calendar
outputs.desc: Schedule of workshops and seminars for the academic year

outputs.name: session-outlines
outputs.desc: Outline for each workshop session

process: Select 8-12 workshop topics from the priority list
Design each session with objectives, activities, and takeaways
Schedule across the academic year avoiding peak grading periods
Identify facilitators for each session

steps.description: Create peer observation and feedback protocols for ongoing teaching improvement.

outputs.name: observation-protocol
outputs.desc: Structured peer observation form and process

outputs.name: feedback-guidelines
outputs.desc: Guidelines for providing constructive peer feedback

process: Define the observation criteria aligned to teaching standards
Create the observation form with structured and open-ended sections
Write guidelines for pre-observation meeting, observation, and debrief
Pilot the protocol with volunteer pairs

steps.description: Design the teaching portfolio process for faculty to document and reflect on their practice.

outputs.name: portfolio-template
outputs.desc: Template for the teaching portfolio

outputs.name: portfolio-guidelines
outputs.desc: Instructions and examples for building the portfolio

process: Define the portfolio components (philosophy, evidence, reflections, goals)
Create the template with sections and prompts
Provide annotated examples of strong portfolios
Establish the review and feedback cycle

steps.description: Establish the faculty mentoring program pairing experienced and new faculty.

inputs.name: faculty-roster
inputs.desc: List of faculty with roles and experience levels

outputs.name: mentoring-plan
outputs.desc: Mentoring program structure, pairings, and expectations

outputs.name: mentoring-agreement
outputs.desc: Template agreement between mentor and mentee

process: Define eligibility and matching criteria
Create the mentoring agreement template
Schedule the program timeline (orientation, check-ins, wrap-up)
Plan the recognition and incentive structure

steps.description: Measure the impact of the faculty development program on teaching quality.

outputs.name: impact-report
outputs.desc: Analysis of program impact on teaching quality

outputs.name: faculty-development-plan
outputs.desc: Updated plan for next cycle based on findings

process: Compare pre- and post-program student evaluation scores
Analyze participation rates and faculty satisfaction surveys
Review teaching portfolio growth over the program period
Produce the impact report and updated development plan

description: Conduct an academic program review using enrollment data, stakeholder feedback, and peer comparison.

steps.description: Collect quantitative program data: enrollment, retention, graduation, and employment rates.

inputs.name: program-name
inputs.desc: Name and level of the academic program under review

inputs.name: review-period
inputs.desc: Time range for the review (e.g., past 5 years)

outputs.name: program-metrics
outputs.desc: Quantitative metrics over the review period

outputs.name: trend-analysis
outputs.desc: Trend analysis of key metrics over time

process: Pull enrollment, retention, and graduation data from the registrar
Collect employment and further education data from alumni surveys
Calculate year-over-year trends for each metric
Produce the metrics summary and trend analysis

steps.description: Gather feedback from students, alumni, employers, and faculty on the program.

outputs.name: feedback-summary
outputs.desc: Aggregated feedback by stakeholder group

outputs.name: common-themes
outputs.desc: Recurring themes across stakeholder groups

process: Survey current students on curriculum, teaching, and resources
Survey alumni on career preparation and program relevance
Interview employers on graduate readiness
Collect faculty reflections on curriculum and resources

steps.description: Compare the program against peer and aspirant programs at other institutions.

outputs.name: peer-comparison
outputs.desc: Comparison of metrics and curriculum against peer programs

outputs.name: competitive-position
outputs.desc: Assessment of the program's competitive standing

process: Identify 5-8 peer programs at comparable institutions
Compare enrollment, graduation rates, and employment outcomes
Compare curriculum structure and specializations
Assess competitive position and differentiators

steps.description: Assess curriculum relevance and rigor against industry needs and disciplinary standards.

outputs.name: relevance-assessment
outputs.desc: Assessment of curriculum currency and rigor

outputs.name: update-recommendations
outputs.desc: Specific curriculum updates recommended

process: Map current curriculum to industry competency requirements
Identify outdated or missing topics
Assess rigor and depth against disciplinary expectations
Produce specific update recommendations

steps.description: Write the program review report synthesizing all findings into strengths, weaknesses, and recommendations.

outputs.name: program-review-report
outputs.desc: Complete program review report

outputs.name: action-plan
outputs.desc: Prioritized action plan with owners and timelines

process: Synthesize quantitative and qualitative findings
Identify program strengths and areas for improvement
Develop specific, actionable recommendations
Create the action plan with responsible parties and deadlines

description: Set up a research mentoring program from goal definition through matching, milestones, and evaluation.

steps.description: Define the goals and expectations for the research mentoring program.

inputs.name: program-context
inputs.desc: Department or institution context for the mentoring program

inputs.name: participant-pool
inputs.desc: Description of potential mentors and mentees

outputs.name: mentoring-goals
outputs.desc: Defined goals for the mentoring program

outputs.name: mentoring-expectations
outputs.desc: Expectations document for mentors and mentees

process: Define program goals (research skill development, publication, grant writing)
Set expectations for meeting frequency and duration
Define mentor responsibilities (feedback, networking, career guidance)
Define mentee responsibilities (preparation, follow-through, communication)

steps.description: Match mentors with mentees based on research interests, methodology, and compatibility.

inputs.name: participant-pool
inputs.desc: Available mentors and mentees with research profiles

inputs.name: mentoring-goals
inputs.desc: Defined goals for the mentoring program

outputs.name: matching-results
outputs.desc: Proposed mentor-mentee pairs with rationale

outputs.name: backup-matches
outputs.desc: Alternative pairings if primary matches decline

process: Collect research interest and methodology profiles from all participants
Score compatibility on research overlap, methodology, and availability
Propose primary and backup matches
Allow participants to review and confirm their matches

steps.description: Create the mentoring agreement defining goals, schedule, and deliverables for each pair.

outputs.name: signed-agreements
outputs.desc: Mentoring agreements signed by each pair

outputs.name: milestone-schedule
outputs.desc: Timeline of milestones and check-ins

process: Have each pair discuss and agree on specific goals
Set the meeting schedule (frequency, format, duration)
Define the milestones and deliverables for the mentoring period
Sign the agreement and register with the program coordinator

steps.description: Track progress on mentoring milestones and provide mid-program check-ins.

outputs.name: milestone-status
outputs.desc: Status of each pair's progress against milestones

outputs.name: mid-program-feedback
outputs.desc: Feedback from mentors and mentees at midpoint

process: Collect progress updates from each pair at scheduled check-ins
Identify pairs falling behind or encountering problems
Provide support or mediation for struggling pairs
Compile the mid-program status report

steps.description: Evaluate the mentoring program outcomes and produce the final report.

inputs.name: milestone-status
inputs.desc: Final status of each pair's progress

outputs.name: mentoring-evaluation
outputs.desc: Evaluation of program outcomes and satisfaction

outputs.name: mentoring-program-document
outputs.desc: Final program document with recommendations for next cycle

process: Survey mentors and mentees on satisfaction and goal achievement
Assess research outputs (publications, presentations, grants submitted)
Identify program strengths and areas for improvement
Produce the evaluation report and recommendations

description: Design a competency-based assessment system with performance indicators, evidence collection, and assessor training.

steps.description: Define the competencies and performance indicators for the program or role.

inputs.name: program-scope
inputs.desc: Program, role, or profession being assessed

inputs.name: standards-reference
inputs.desc: Professional or accreditation standards to align with

outputs.name: competency-framework
outputs.desc: List of competencies with performance indicators

outputs.name: proficiency-levels

Define proficiency levels (novice, developing, proficient, expert)

steps.description: Create assessment tasks that allow learners to demonstrate each competency.

outputs.name: assessment-tasks
outputs.desc: Tasks aligned to each competency with instructions

outputs.name: task-rubrics

Align each task to one or more competencies
Write scoring rubrics mapping task performance to proficiency levels
Review tasks for fairness and accessibility

steps.description: Design the evidence collection process for documenting competency attainment.

outputs.name: evidence-portfolio-template
outputs.desc: Template for the learner evidence portfolio

outputs.name: collection-procedures
outputs.desc: Procedures for collecting and storing evidence

process: Define acceptable evidence types per competency (artifacts, observations, reflections)
Create the portfolio template with sections for each competency
Design the submission and review workflow
Set policies for evidence quality and authenticity

steps.description: Build the competency tracking system to record and visualize learner progress.

outputs.name: tracking-system
outputs.desc: Configured system for tracking competency progress

description: Plan the adoption of a new educational technology from needs identification through full rollout.

steps.description: Identify the pedagogical need that technology could address.

inputs.name: teaching-challenge
inputs.desc: Description of the teaching or learning challenge

outputs.name: need-statement
outputs.desc: Clear statement of the pedagogical need

outputs.name: success-criteria
outputs.desc: Criteria for evaluating whether the technology addresses the need

process: Analyze the teaching challenge and its root cause
Determine if technology can address the root cause (vs. pedagogical redesign)
Write the need statement with measurable success criteria
Confirm alignment with institutional technology strategy

steps.description: Evaluate candidate tools against features, accessibility, privacy, and cost criteria.

inputs.name: need-statement
inputs.desc: Clear statement of the pedagogical need

outputs.name: tool-shortlist
outputs.desc: Top 2-3 tools with evaluation scores

outputs.name: evaluation-matrix
outputs.desc: Detailed scoring matrix for all candidates

process: Identify 5-8 candidate tools through research and recommendations
Score each tool on functionality, accessibility (WCAG), privacy (FERPA/GDPR), and cost
Check vendor stability, support quality, and integration capabilities
Select the top 2-3 finalists

steps.description: Pilot the top candidate with a small group of faculty and students.

outputs.name: pilot-results
outputs.desc: Usage data and feedback from the pilot

outputs.name: selected-tool
outputs.desc: Final tool selection based on pilot results

process: Recruit 3-5 faculty volunteers for a one-semester pilot
Provide initial training and support during the pilot
Collect usage data, student feedback, and faculty observations
Evaluate against success criteria and select the tool

steps.description: Develop training materials and support resources for faculty adoption.

inputs.name: selected-tool
inputs.desc: The tool selected from the pilot

outputs.name: training-materials
outputs.desc: Guides, videos, and reference materials for faculty

outputs.name: support-plan
outputs.desc: Ongoing support plan (help desk, office hours, peer support)

process: Create getting-started guides and video tutorials
Document common use cases and best practices from the pilot
Set up the help desk workflow and FAQ
Identify faculty champions for peer support

steps.description: Plan and execute the full institutional rollout of the selected technology.

outputs.name: rollout-timeline
outputs.desc: Phased rollout schedule by department or program

outputs.name: adoption-plan
outputs.desc: Complete technology adoption plan document

process: Design a phased rollout schedule (early adopters, then all departments)
Set adoption targets and monitoring checkpoints
Plan the communication campaign for faculty and students
Produce the complete adoption plan with success metrics
